subject: Scaling from composable to reserved — feature bundling & rollback concerns
messages:
From: Jorge Silva <jorge@opswell.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: opswell-sales@opswell.io
Date: 2027-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Scaling from composable to reserved — feature bundling & rollback concerns

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Opswell is ready to talk about moving a portion of our workload off the composable model and into a reserved pool to get predictable throughput for our core inference pipelines. Before we lock in procurement I need clarity on a few packaging items:

- Feature bundling: we rely on Advanced Routing, persistent KV cache, and routing fallbacks — can these be retained verbatim on a Reserved SKU or are they gated into a different feature bundle?
- Step-up credits and proration: if we commit mid-billing cycle, how would usage credits / overage invoicing be handled?
- Rollback / fallback: if the Reserved pilot underperforms, what is the rollback process and associated fees? Is there a grace window?
- Billing examples: would appreciate a worked example turning our current 200k monthly tokens and 3000 embeddings into a Reserved throughput/seat commitment.

I've attached our last invoice and a short usage export to help with sizing (opswell_invoice_may2027.pdf, opswell_usage_q1.csv).

Can we schedule 30 minutes today or tomorrow to align a Mutual Action Plan and the procurement timeline?

Regards,
Jorge Silva
Head of Infrastructure
Opswell Inc.
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jorge Silva <jorge@opswell.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Scaling from composable to reserved — feature bundling & rollback concerns

Jorge — thanks for the details and the attachments, that makes sizing straightforward. Looping in Kimberly (CS) and Ben (Sales Ops) to cover feature mapping + contract mechanics. Quick summary of the options we recommend: 

Option A — Reserved throughput (predictable latency):
- 3-month pilot reserved pool sized to 120k rps-equivalent; converts to a monthly commit after pilot.
- Feature bundle: dedicated Reserved SKU includes Advanced Routing and KV persistence by default; we can carve out advanced integrations if you need them isolated.
- Credits/proration: we apply a pro-rated credit for the month you convert; any composable overage in the conversion month is credited against the new commitment.

Option B — Hybrid (Composable + Reserved carve):
- Keep lower-priority traffic on composable; move core endpoints to Reserved.
- Billing: split invoice with reserved commitment and composable usage; easier rollback as core remains composable.

Rollback and guardrails:
- Standard rollback window: 60 days from conversion for a full revert with reduced termination fee if usage is below threshold.
- We can include an SLA clause for latency and an automatic fallback to composable if Reserved capacity saturation exceeds the agreed threshold.

Action items I propose before procurement:
1) Quick sizing call (30 min) to confirm pool size and feature scopes — I have 11:30am and 3:00pm PT today.
2) Draft MAP (attached: draft_map.pdf) with milestones, procurement steps, and rollback gates.
3) Ben will provide a worked-pricing example and the formal pricing grid.

If those time windows don't work, suggest two slots and we'll adjust.

— Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Ben here — attaching the concrete pricing artifacts you asked for. Summary bullets to make procurement easier: 
- Reserved pricing example: converting your 200k tokens/month + 3k embeddings maps to a Reserved pool we estimate at 0.8x of our medium slot — monthly commit = $22,500/mo (example).
- Conversion credit: we grant a one-time credit equal to the prorated composable spend in the conversion month (applies if you convert before the 15th of the billing cycle).
- Rollback fees: full rollback permitted within 60 days with a reduced administrative fee (2% of the remaining committed months) if usage falls below 75% of the committed throughput. After 60 days standard early termination clauses apply.
- Feature bundling: Advanced Routing and persistent KV cache remain in the Reserved feature bundle. Any custom plugin work or third-party connectors are scoped as professional services (separate SOW).

Attached: reserved_pricing_grid.xlsx, rollback_terms.docx

Concrete worked example (illustrative):
- Current monthly composable spend: $18,200 (May 2027 invoice)
- Proposed Reserved commit: $22,500/mo for predictable latency and 30% lower per-token cost at scale
- Conversion credit applied in month 1: $18,200 * (days remaining / 30) -> credited toward first Reserved invoice

If this looks right we'll produce a short MAP and a DocuSign-ready amendment for procurement.

— Ben Carter
Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
